land.text: Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy (Milan), whose Lombard and Venetian lands Austria occupied in April 1814 and received in 1815; the page's infobox names the Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic) and the Republic of San Marco as predecessors

predecessors.note: Cliopatria files the Napoleonic Kingdom under 'Italian Republic'.

land.text: Lombardy up to the Mincio, ceded 1859 (via France) at the Treaty of Zurich; the fortresses of Mantua and Peschiera stayed Austrian

successors.note: The state continued with Venetia and Mantua until 1866.

land.text: Venetia and Mantua, ceded 1866 (to France, then to Italy), annexed by plebiscite 21-22 October 1866

capitals.name: Milan
capitals.note: Page infobox: capital Milan 1815-1859; viceroys 'resident in Milan and Venice'. The seat moved to Venice in 1859 (the page: 'the capital was relocated to Venice').

correction.text: Lombardy and the Veneto of 1815: the Milan and Venice governments, i.e. the Habsburg gains of the Final Act (Lombardy incl. Mantua, Valtellina; Venetia incl. Friuli west of the Isonzo)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). Gazetteer area of Lombardy+Veneto+Udine+Pordenone is about 49,600 km2 against the infobox's 46,782 km2 for 1852 (ratio 1.06). The page names no boundary; the modern regions are my reading of 'Lombardy' and 'Venetia'. 1848-49 (insurgent months) is carried by ledger events, not by a separate shape.

correction.text: Venetia, western Friuli and Mantua: Lombardy kept only the fortresses of Mantua (and Peschiera) after the 1859 cession up to the Mincio

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the Treaty of Zurich only Venetia, western Friuli and the Mantua fortress remained. The page: Austria 'had to cede Lombardy up to the Mincio River, except for the fortresses of Mantua and Peschiera'; the Second War page says 'excluding only the Austrian fortresses of Mantua and Legnago' (Lombardy to France, then to Sardinia). Shape = Venetia plus Mantova province as a generous reading of the Mincio line.

region.text: Lombardy and the Veneto of 1815: the Milan and Venice governments, i.e. the Habsburg gains of the Final Act (Lombardy incl. Mantua, Valtellina; Venetia incl. Friuli west of the Isonzo)

ledger.note: 1815: the Congress of Vienna creates the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia for the Austrian crown. 'It was created in 1815 by resolution of the Congress of Vienna' (infobox dates it 9 June 1815). The page gives no boundary; the region is my reading.

region.text: Milan and Como, after the Five Days: 'After a popular revolution on 22 March 1848, known as the Five Days of Milan' the Austrians fled; 'Milan became the capital of a Governo Provvisorio della Lombardia'

ledger.note: 22 March 1848: Milan rises and Radetzky retreats to the Quadrilateral. The Lombard provisional government has no dossier (5 months; it voted for union with Piedmont on 8 June 1848, see kingdom-of-sardinia). From the First Italian War page (second page): Radetzky 'was forced to abandon the city' and the Austrians fell back into the Quadrilateral fortresses (Peschiera, Verona, Mantua, Legnago) from 23 March; Como also revolted.

region.text: the Veneto towns that sided with Venice in 1848: 'Belluno, Padua, Rovigo, Treviso, Udine, and Vicenza' (Verona stayed Austrian)

ledger.note: March 1848: Venice proclaims the Republic of San Marco and the Veneto towns follow. 'independence was declared on 22 March 1848'; the republic 'extended into most of Venetia'; the towns that sided with the lagoon included 'Belluno, Padua, Rovigo, Treviso, Udine, and Vicenza'; Verona stayed Austrian. The page does not date each town.

region.text: the Lombard plain and the Quadrilateral: 'On 23 March, the Kingdom of Sardinia declared war on the Austrian Empire'; advance guards 'crossed the Ticino on 25-26 March'

ledger.note: 23-26 March 1848: Sardinia invades Lombardy. 'On 23 March, the Kingdom of Sardinia declared war on the Austrian Empire.' Advance guards crossed the Ticino on 25-26 March, the main army on 29 March.

region.text: Udine, 'which surrendered on 22 April after an artillery bombardment'

ledger.note: 22-23 April 1848: Nugent's corps takes Udine. First Italian War page: 'Udine which surrendered on 22 April after an artillery bombardment'; the Austrians occupied it on 23 April. Palmanova (Udine province) held out to 24 June. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: added/changed from the First Italian War page.]

region.text: Belluno: 'the Austrians entered Belluno on 5 May'

ledger.note: 5 May 1848: Nugent's corps enters Belluno. First Italian War page: 'the Austrians entered Belluno on 5 May'. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: added/changed from the First Italian War page.]

region.text: Vicenza, Padua, Treviso and Palmanova (Udine province)

ledger.note: 11-24 June 1848: Austria retakes the Veneto towns. 'Padua and Treviso fell on 13 June 1848, Vicenza surrendered on 11 June, and Palmanova fell on 24 June'. Osoppo held out until 13 October 1848. The page does not name the captor in these sentences; the Austrian counter-offensive is my reading.

region.text: Rovigo, the rest of the Veneto mainland held by the insurgents until the armistice

ledger.note: By 9 August 1848 only Venice remained in insurgent hands. The First Italian War page: Venice was 'the only city in Lombardy-Venetia which remained in the hands of the insurgents' after the armistice. It does not date the return of Rovigo; this event bridges that silence. Belluno is a separate May event. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: added/changed from the First Italian War page.]

9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice returns Lombardy. 'Radetzky and Salasco concluded an armistice on 9 August 1848, requiring Piedmont to withdraw from Lombardy-Venetia'; the Austrians entered Milan on 6 August (Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia page: 'entered Milan (6 August) and Venice (24 August 1849)').

region.text: the Lombard plain and the Quadrilateral

ledger.note: 9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice ends the first campaign (Custoza 25 July). The fighting resumed on 23 March 1849 at Novara, on Piedmontese soil.

region.text: the fortress of Osoppo, held by the insurgents

ledger.note: 13 October 1848: Osoppo, the last mainland stronghold, falls. The page: 'Osoppo held out until 13 October 1848'.

region.text: Venice, the last insurgent city: 'Terms were agreed on 22 August'; 'Radetzky's entrance to Venice on 27 August'

ledger.note: 22-27 August 1849: Venice surrenders. 'Terms were agreed on 22 August'; 'Radetzky's entrance to Venice on 27 August marked the complete surrender of Venice'. The Kingdom page gives 24 August 1849 for the entry; the Republic page 27 August (its lead says 28).

region.text: Lombardy west of the Mincio, where the Franco-Sardinian armies fought

ledger.note: 26 April 1859: the Second Italian War begins. 'Upon Sardinia's refusal, the war began on 26 April', after Austria's ultimatum of 23 April; Magenta 4 June, Solferino 24 June.
11-12 July 1859: the Armistice of Villafranca. 'The two emperors met on 11 July at Villafranca di Verona and the armistice was signed on the following day.'

region.text: Lombardy: 'Most of Lombardy, with its capital, Milan, excluding only the Austrian fortresses of Mantua and Legnago'; the Kingdom page: 'cede Lombardy up to the Mincio River, except for the fortresses of Mantua and Peschiera' (Mantova kept, as in the 1859 keyframe)

ledger.note: Nov 1859: Austria cedes Lombardy. The Kingdom page's infobox: 'Lombardy ceded to France: 10 November 1859'; Austria 'by the Treaty of Zurich had to cede Lombardy up to the Mincio River, except for the fortresses of Mantua and Peschiera'. The Second War page dates the treaty 11 November and says France then gave Lombardy to Sardinia (counterpart kingdom-of-sardinia; France only the intermediary). [Reviewer eu-20-x: region now Lombardy minus Mantova, to agree with the 1859 keyframe, which keeps Mantova.]
1859: the capital moves from Milan to Venice. 'while the capital was relocated to Venice'; infobox Milan 1815-1859, Venice 1859-1866.

region.text: Veneto and the Mincio: 'Three days later, Italy declared war on Austria and started military operations on 23 June' (infobox 20 June)

ledger.note: 20-23 June 1866: Italy opens the Third War of Independence; Custoza on 24 June is an Austrian victory, Garibaldi's volunteers reach Bezzecca (Trentino) on 21 July and Italian forces Romans d'Isonzo on 26 July, 'the maximum Italian advance into Friuli'.
12 August 1866: the Armistice of Cormons ends the fighting in Italy ('the Armistice of Cormons signed on 12 August').

region.text: Venetia, western Friuli and Mantua: Lombardy kept only the fortresses of Mantua (and Peschiera) after the 1859 cession up to the Mincio

ledger.note: October 1866: Venetia passes to Italy. 'the Treaty of Vienna on 3 October 1866'; Napoleon III 'ceded Venetia to Italy on 19 October'; 'The plebiscite was held on 21 and 22 October', 'consisting of modern Veneto, parts of Friuli and the city of Mantua'. The Kingdom page's infobox dates the treaty 12 October 1866 and lists the successors Second French Empire and Kingdom of Italy.

region.text: Venetia, western Friuli and Mantua: Lombardy kept only the fortresses of Mantua (and Peschiera) after the 1859 cession up to the Mincio

ledger.note: 1866: the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia ends. Infobox 'Treaty of Vienna: 12 October 1866'; Venetia and Mantua 'fell to the Kingdom of Italy ... by the 1866 Peace of Prague' and 'a plebiscite marked the Italian annexation on 21-22 October 1866'.

wars.name: First Italian War of Independence

zones.text: the Veneto towns that sided with Venice in 1848: 'Belluno, Padua, Rovigo, Treviso, Udine, and Vicenza' (Verona stayed Austrian)

wars.outcome: Austria crushed the Lombard and Venetian risings and Sardinia's two campaigns (Custoza 25 July 1848, armistice 9 August; Novara 23 March 1849); Venice surrendered in August 1849. No border changed: the Peace of Milan (6 August 1849) only imposed a 65 million franc indemnity.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Franco-Sardinian victory at Magenta (4 June) and Solferino (24 June); armistice of Villafranca 11-12 July; Treaty of Zurich: Lombardy to Sardinia via France, Mantua and Legnago (Peschiera) kept by Austria.

wars.name: Third Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Italy lost Custoza (24 June) and Lissa (20 July) but obtained Venetia and Mantua through Prussia's victory: Armistice of Cormons 12 August, Peace of Prague, Treaty of Vienna 3 October, cession through France 19 October, plebiscite 21-22 October 1866.

certainty.note: The kingdom's frontiers follow the Congress of Vienna settlement and the provincial boundaries; the page gives no frontier text, so the sharp level rests on the treaty origin.
The insurgents' holdings changed week by week (Milan, Venice, the Veneto towns, Osoppo); the Quadrilateral stayed Austrian throughout.
The 1859 Treaty of Zurich line (the Mincio) and the 1866 Treaty of Vienna cession are treaty lines.

notes: New dossier: Cliopatria has no Lombardy-Venetia row; the Austrian Empire row (austrian-empire_1815 .. 1866) draws the territory inside the empire, so the renderer must not double-colour it: either this dossier overrides that part or it is a vassal-tint entity of the empire (type is 'state' because the page calls it a kingdom, its emperor-king aside). Rulers omitted: the kings were the emperors of Austria (see austrian-empire); the page lists only viceroys and governors-general (Bellegarde 1815-16, Anton Victor 1816-18, Rainer Joseph 1818-48, Radetzky 1848-57, Maximilian 1857-59). Predecessor handover is Cliopatria's 'Italian Republic' 1813 shape (the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy). Counterpart 'Provisional Government of Milan' (March-August 1848, five months) has no dossier and is not planned. Dates differ between pages: Zurich 10 vs 11 November 1859; Treaty of Vienna 3 vs 12 October 1866; Venice surrender 22/24/27/28 August 1849. 'Veneto', 'Udine', 'Pordenone' and 'Lombardy' resolve through the gazetteer's Italian provinces; Friuli east of the Judrio and the Valtellina detail were not checked against a page. Not opened: Congress of Vienna Final Act (page budget).
